title: 3 Claude Code commands most people never use: /compact to sh

plan.visualBrief: A glass Claude Code window with three files turning red; /rewind is typed and a teal U-turn arrow sweeps up over them as they turn green.

scenes.vo: Claude Code just broke three files? One command undoes it.

plan.visualBrief: A big purple glass tile counts up to 3 over blurred Claude Code docs, and three empty numbered slots drop into the dock below.

scenes.vo: It's one of three Claude Code commands most people never use.

plan.visualBrief: Light scene: /rewind fills dock slot 1 and is typed into the Claude Code window, the three red files roll back one by one, then all turn green.

scenes.vo: First, slash rewind. Type it, and Claude Code undoes its last changes. Those three broken files? Clean again.

plan.visualBrief: /compact fills slot 2; a scrolling chat with a red 186k context meter squeezes into one short Summary block while the blue thread line from start to now stays unbroken.

scenes.vo: Second, slash compact. When a session gets long and heavy, it shrinks it down, without losing the thread of what you're building.

plan.visualBrief: Big Shift and Tab keys press down and plan mode turns on; a Claude Code window rises with a numbered plan, and the files below snap padlocked.

scenes.vo: Third, plan mode. Press Shift Tab, and Claude shows you its plan first. Not a single file is touched until you're happy with it.

plan.visualBrief: Light scene: the finished three-command list collapses into the dock as a comment bubble pops up asking for more tips, and a big orange Follow button pulses.

scenes.vo: Drop a comment if you want more Claude Code tips like these, and follow so you don't miss the next one.

storyPlan.premise: 3 Claude Code commands most people never use: /compact to shrink a long session without losing the thread, /rewind to undo the last changes, and plan mode (Shift+Tab) to see the plan before any file is touched. Show each one working.
